gap: No result ChatGPT got states that 'power station or generator' doesn't have to be one or the other: each maker supports only specific pairings, with stated limits. EcoFlow's Smart Generator 3000 (Dual Fuel) can auto start and stop only with the DELTA 3, DELTA 3 Plus and DELTA 3 Ultra Plus. Anker's F3800 Plus takes a 240 V gas generator only through the Anker SOLIX Generator Adapter, and only as a single unit. A 120 V generator feeding the F3800 Plus must give pure sine wave power under 5% THD. A Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 needs a source of at least 1,100 W to charge.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search and got no results, so there were no rival pages to compare against. Its answer treats the two as an either/or choice with a generic table. It never says that a battery and a gas generator can be paired, which pairings each maker supports, or the limits each maker states (adapter needed, single unit only, pure sine and THD rule, minimum generator watts, no shipping to California).
decides: This changes the pick for home-backup shoppers who need long runtime. Instead of buying either one, they can pair a battery with a generator the maker supports. For automatic hybrid backup at a low cost, the EcoFlow DELTA 3 or DELTA 3 Plus with the Smart Generator 3000 (Dual Fuel, $689 on EcoFlow US today) is the only listed pairing where the generator starts and stops itself, but it can't ship to California. For whole-home 240 V use through a transfer switch, the Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus takes a 240 V generator through Anker's adapter. A shopper who wants a camping-size unit charged by a cheap open-frame generator should first check that the generator gives clean power and enough watts: Anker says pure sine under 5% THD for 120 V generators, and Jackery says at least 1,100 W for the Explorer 1000 v2.

findings.label: Generator input requirements and exclusions
findings.value: Needs the Anker SOLIX Generator Adapter, and works with a single F3800 Plus only. 240 V generator bypass up to 6,000 W. Generator charging up to 3,300 W on a single unit, or 6,000 W with one or more expansion batteries.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Generator Input Adapter
findings.note: Page text: '*Anker SOLIX Generator Adapter required and only support single F3800 Plus unit.' The spec table marks generator bypass 'Yes' for the F3800 Plus and 'No' for the original F3800. The generator connects to the 'HPP & Generator Adapter Port'.

findings.label: 120 V generator power quality requirement
findings.value: Pure sine wave, THD under 5%. On a 120 V generator, the TT-30R works on the L1 phase only and is capped at 3,000 W.
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX F3800 Plus Portable Power Station
findings.note: Also stated on the adapter page. Other limits from the product page: 'Designed for North American Power Standards Only.' 'The 240V output cannot be used while the device is charging via 120V AC.' Expands with up to 6 BP3800 batteries (3.84 kWh each). The product FAQ says it works with the Home Power Panel, a transfer switch or inlet box, and the Double Power Hub.

findings.label: Minimum source power for AC input (sets the generator size)
findings.value: 1,100 W. AC input 100–120 V, 60 Hz, 15 A max, 1,000 W ± 50 W max input. Expansion batteries and parallel operation are not supported.
findings.source_title: Explorer 1000 V2 Basic Information – Jackery FAQ
findings.note: Jackery's FAQ lists 'Minimum power required for AC input: 1100W'. It applies this to charging from another Jackery station ('AC output meets or exceeds 1100W + 50W'). The page doesn't mention generators, so the 1,100 W floor is the source requirement for any AC supply, not a generator-specific rule from Jackery.
